subject: Security exhibit — audit phases, evidence ownership, and pen-test window
messages:
From: Jamie Wu <jamie.wu@atlashealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Redwood security exhibit (SOC 2 evidence cadence + pen-test window)

Hi Michael / Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the draft security exhibit. A few follow-ups from our side as we run this across our compliance and infra teams: 

1) SOC 2 evidence cadence — do you expect to provide an ongoing quarterly evidence bundle (logs/config snapshots) or only an annual report plus ad-hoc evidence on request? Our auditors usually expect quarterly evidence for critical controls.

2) Pen test language — we need clarity on what you consider in-scope (prod only? staging?), the notification window you require, and whether we get a short period for remediation before any findings are considered final.

3) Audit rights — the MSA currently references broad "reasonable access" wording; procurement prefers explicit limits (scope, duration, remote vs on-site). Can Redwood propose tightened language?

Attached: ATH-Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v1.docx (our redlines in comments).

Can we set a short sync this week to agree a path forward? Ideally we lock the exhibit alongside the order form signature.

Thanks,
Jamie Wu
Sr. Security Manager, Atlas Health
Attachments: ATH-Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v1.docx (docx)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Wu <jamie.wu@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Redwood security exhibit (SOC 2 evidence cadence + pen-test window)

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. Karthik, Laura and Irene are looped for scope and legal. Quick answers inline, and I attached our proposed redlined exhibit for your review (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v1_redlines.docx).

- SOC 2 evidence cadence: We provide the annual SOC 2 Type II report by default. For customers that need more frequent operational evidence, we offer a quarterly evidence bundle (control mappings, selected logs, change summaries) as an add-on to the Order Form. For Atlas Health, we can include the quarterly bundle for the life of the contract (recommendation).

- Pen test window: We support customer-led pen testing against production with the following guardrails: 30-day advance notice, a mutually agreed test window (max 14 consecutive days), and a pre-approved scope limited to listed endpoints/services. Redwood requires a single technical point-of-contact and a remediation period of 10 business days before formal findings are closed.

- Audit rights / "reasonable access": We can narrow the MSA language to: (i) audit rights apply only to in-scope systems enumerated in the security exhibit; (ii) audits are limited to remote document and evidence review plus one on-site visit per 12-month period with 30 days' notice; and (iii) any on-site access must be scheduled during normal business hours and be limited to read-only observation of systems. Laura — suggested alternate contract language attached below.

Next steps I propose:
- Michael to share Redwood redlines (attached).
- Two 30-min follow-ups: (1) technical alignment (Karthik + Atlas infra) and (2) legal alignment (Laura + Irene + Atlas procurement).
- Incorporate agreed language into the final Order Form so signatures can proceed.

Available for quick sync today 2–4pm PT or tomorrow morning.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v1_redlines.docx (docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Wu <jamie.wu@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Redwood security exhibit (SOC 2 evidence cadence + pen-test window)

Jamie — quick technical clarifications from infra:

1) Scope: We recommend the pen test be scoped to production control plane and inference endpoints only. Non-prod (staging/dev) is strongly discouraged for external testing due to shared infra and intermittent data.

2) Notice & coordination: 30 days' notice is standard. We'll ask for a test plan from your vendor (IP ranges, tool list, target endpoints) 10 business days before the window. Redwood will provide a temporary read-only monitoring access artifact for the test period to capture logs.

3) Blast radius minimization: No privileged credential harvesting or attempts at privilege escalation across customer-managed integrations. If the test requires social-engineering or human-factor attempts, that must be explicitly excluded unless pre-authorized and supervised.

I've uploaded a short mutual action plan spreadsheet with the proposed timeline and owners: MAP-AtlasHealth-Redwood.xlsx. If the timeline looks good we'll lock the 30-day notice + 14-day window cadence in Clause 5.3 of the exhibit.

—Karthik
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-AtlasHealth-Redwood.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Wu <jamie.wu@atlashealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Redwood security exhibit (SOC 2 evidence cadence + pen-test window)

Jamie / Michael — Laura from Legal. I reviewed the draft MSA/exhibit redlines and propose the following concrete contract language to replace the current broad audit rights clause: 

"Audit Rights: Customer may conduct an audit of Redwood's in-scope systems as defined in Exhibit A (In-Scope Systems) no more than once every 12 months. All audit activity shall be limited to (i) remote document review, (ii) remote evidence collection (logs, configuration snapshots), and (iii) one on-site visit per 12-month period, each with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice. On-site visits shall be limited to business hours and to read-only observation. Any audit findings that require remediation shall be documented, and Redwood shall be provided with a reasonable period (not less than ten (10) business days) to remediate before findings are considered final. Third-party auditors are permitted provided they execute Redwood's standard NDA and scope-of-work non-disclosure appendix in advance."

Please note: we cannot accept unlimited forensic access or unrestricted production access. If Atlas Health needs broader access, we can accommodate via an audit services add-on that includes a managed evidence runbook and a dedicated compliance liaison. Pricing for the add-on is on the MAP.

If this language looks acceptable to Atlas, Michael can incorporate it into the redlined exhibit and we can route a new copy of the Order Form for signature.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

From: Jamie Wu <jamie.wu@atlashealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: 2026-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Redwood security exhibit (SOC 2 evidence cadence + pen-test window)

Thanks, team — that all makes sense. Procurement and security are aligned on the proposed language and the quarterly evidence bundle as an add-on works for us. Two small asks before we finalize: 

1) Can you attach the final redlined exhibit with the audit clause Laura proposed so our counsel can do a quick thumbs-up?
2) We'll need a DocuSign-ready Order Form that includes the quarterly evidence add-on and the MAP entry for pen-test scheduling.

If those two items land today we can circulate for signature and get a target pen-test window into next month's calendar.

Appreciate it — Jamie
Sr. Security Manager, Atlas Health
